title: Sweep what students see for authoring leftovers
statement: Sweep everything a student is served, as it renders, for authoring leftovers such as working notes, markup tokens, escaped characters and placeholder codes, which instructions alone don't prevent.
example: In one course, 144 items showed escaped characters in their feedback.
detail: Render audits in a reading project found faults that a structural audit could not see, only the rendered page (`grade3-reading/artifacts/alpha-read-packager/v2_final_package/docs/SUMMARY_AGENT.qmd`, line 134). Two passages showed a literal heading token in their text, traced to builders that wrapped every block as a paragraph (`grade3-reading/artifacts/alpha-read-packager/FIX_LIST.md`, line 114), and 144 items showed escaped characters in their feedback (`grade3-reading/artifacts/alpha-read-packager/v2_final_package/docs/SUMMARY_AGENT.qmd`, line 138). A quality-gate report across several courses found two items whose passage was only a standards code, so they could not be answered (`grade3-reading/artifacts/alpha-read-packager/v2_final_package/docs/COURSE_QUALITY_GATE_REPORT.md`, lines 434-435).

evidence.quote: Both leak the literal authoring token `HEADING:` into student-visible body text.
the "looks broken" class the structural audit can't see
passage text is literally the CCSS code string `RI.3.8`. No passage. Unanswerable.
Note: Do not include headers or titles in the explanation. Just use new paragraphs.
Text now draws on a separate transparent overlay, and the internal script label for scene 5 has been removed from the student-facing frame.
image-slot placeholders ("Drop a cartoon of William Shakespeare")
Separate issue on the same screen: the template placeholders are visible to the student.
Remove the template placeholders "\[word class\]" and "\[word\]" from anything a student sees, and audit for the same leak elsewhere.
the with-help release message renders as `undefined` when the valve fires.
